newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Rising Taiwan electronic shares defy index.
newsitem.headline: Rising Taiwan electronic shares defy index.

text.p: Several of Taiwan's electronics shares attracted heavy buying in late trade on Tuedsay in an otherwise sluggish market, brokers said.
With 45 minutes of trade remaining, Macronix was up T$0.20 to T$37.50 on heavy volume of 22.05 million shares and Microtek rose T$0.60 to T$43.50 with 20 million shares traded.

First International Computer, Taiwan's second largest computer maker, gained T$0.60 to T$38.90, also in active trade involving 12.12 million shares. The overall index was down 44 points or 0.68 percent at 6,380.72.
Electronics firms made up six of the 10 most heavily-traded shares in the late session.

"In a down market like this, the only shares investors would buy are the ones seen as having a clear, sound outlook, and electronic shares naturally become the focus," said Joe Chiou of Taiwan Securities Investment.
Analysts have said they expect export orders for electronic products to rise in the fourth quarter of 1996.
